subject: Varied trap usage and nonspatial openCR models - does it matter?

messages.author: b97acb36e359be28
messages.subject: Varied trap usage and nonspatial openCR models - does it matter?
parts: Hello, I have been using the secr package for some time and just recently have been fitting nonspatial models using openCR. Because I have formatted my data for secr models in the past, I have been using that capthist data format for openCR as well. I have noticed that varying the trap usage in the capthist does not have any effect on the nonspatial model results. I understand that the spatial component does not matter, but I would think that the total sample effort would still be important. My main question is whether or not there is a way to incorporate varied sampling effort between occasions into openCR? Accompanying question: is my thinking on this is wrong and it is not in fact important to consider this when the spatial component is removed?

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Varied trap usage and nonspatial openCR models - does it matter?
parts:
Interesting. You have a point (known variation in effort should be allowed for in non-spatial open CR) but that doesn't happen because my only mechanism for tracking effort is detector-specific, and detectors do not appear in the non-spatial model. My defence might be that the effect of varying effort is usually minor, but I suppose it matters if you care about the detection parameters themselves (just p, I suppose).

So am I motivated to add a non spatial argument for varying effort, like varying interval length? Not right now, but I could be persuaded. (Maybe there is a workaround using a time covariate for which you fix the coefficient - can't remember if fixing beta parameters is documented!).
Murray
